question: Why does silver chloride turn white in sunlight?

options.text: Due to rusting of silver in the presence of oxygen
Due to decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light.
Due to displacement of silver chloride into silver oxide

solution:
The correct answer is __**Due to decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine by light.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Silver chloride** is a **photosensitive compound**, which means it reacts to light by decomposing.
 
• When silver chloride is exposed to sunlight, the **energy from the light** causes the** compound to break down into silver and chlorine ions.**
 
• The s**ilver ions combine with other substances** in the environment to **form a white precipitate**, which gives the **appearance of the silver chloride turning white**.
 
• This process is reversible, and the white precipitate can turn back into silver chloride when removed from sunlight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Application of this phenomenon**:

 
 
• As this process is reversible, as the grey color can fade when the silver chloride is shielded from light or heated.
 
• This property has **historical significance in photography**, as it was **used in the early photographic process known as the daguerreotype**.
 
 
 
• **Redox reaction:**
 
 
• **Redox reactions are chemical processes involving oxidation and reduction in which the oxidation states of the reactants change.** 
 
• In a chemical reaction, the **material that is being reduced **is referred to as the** oxidizing agent**, and the **substance that is being oxidized** is referred to as the **reducing agent**. 
 
 
 
• **Displacement reaction:**
 
 
• **When an atom in a molecule is displaced by another atom, this is known as a displacement reaction.**
